findings.evidence: PR lines 99-124 define `segClamp = max s_j (min t s_jp1)` and prove ordered membership/endpoint lemmas; Mathlib has `Set.projIcc` as `max a (min b x)` at `Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/ProjIcc.lean:48,60`, endpoint/membership lemmas at lines 66,69,100, and continuity at `Mathlib/Topology/Order/ProjIcc.lean:33`.
findings.fix: Keep the proof-free `segClamp` only if needed for the unordered public left-endpoint lemma, but bridge ordered uses to `Set.projIcc s_j s_jp1 h t` and use `Set.coe_projIcc`, `Set.projIcc_of_mem`, `Set.projIcc_of_right_le`, and `Set.continuous_projIcc`.
findings.issue: The ordered `segClamp` API (`segClamp_mem_Icc`, `segClamp_eq_self`, `segClamp_eq_right`, and ordered continuity uses) reproves Mathlib's closed-interval projection facts for the same `max/min` clamp in all ordered segment contexts.

findings.evidence: PR lines 216-229 prove `∏ j ∈ range k, a (j+1)/a j = a k/a 0`; Mathlib already provides `Finset.prod_range_div` at `Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean:896`, and `Units.mk0` is the standard nonzero-to-unit bridge (`Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Units/Basic.lean:234,279`).
findings.fix: Package the nonzero complex terms as units, apply `Finset.prod_range_div (fun j => Units.mk0 (a j) (ha j ...)) k`, then coerce back to `ℂ` to get the current statement.
findings.issue: `prod_range_div_complex` reproves the standard telescoping range product instead of using Mathlib's `Finset.prod_range_div`.

summary: The PR still rederives existing Mathlib scaffolding for ordered interval projection and telescoping products. These are reuse issues in private proofs, not objections to the new public contour statement itself.
